# Two Balls, One Collision: Setting Up the Forces

<!-- STEP id="the-scenario" -->
Two balls collide head-on and stay in contact for a short time t. Ball A has mass $m_1$ and velocity $u_1$ before the collision, $v_1$ after. Ball B has mass $m_2$ and velocity $u_2$ before, $v_2$ after.

<!-- STEP id="force-on-a" -->
During the collision, ball B pushes on ball A. By the second law, that force is A's mass times A's acceleration — the rate of change of A's momentum:

$$F_{\text{on A}} = \frac{m_1(v_1 - u_1)}{t}$$

<!-- STEP id="force-on-b" -->
At the very same instant, ball A pushes back on ball B, exactly as hard in the opposite sense:

$$F_{\text{on B}} = \frac{m_2(v_2 - u_2)}{t}$$

<!-- STEP id="the-pair" -->
These two forces — B pushing A, A pushing B — are exactly a Newton's-third-law pair: one force on each of two different objects, acting at the same moment.
